biography.plain_text: American oil entrepreneur Lev Herrington Prichard co-founded Anderson-Prichard with J. Steve Anderson in 1919. The business developed oil interests across Oklahoma, Texas and Louisiana and operated a refinery at Cyril. Prichard subsequently bought out his partner and took the company public, remaining its leading figure until his death in 1949.

long_biography.plain_text:
Before becoming an Oklahoma oilman, Lev Prichard worked on his family's Mississippi cotton farm from the age of eight. Fieldwork limited his schooling to four months a year. He worked his way through Mississippi College, graduating in 1906, and then earned a law degree at Millsaps College.

Prichard moved to Oklahoma in 1909, where legal work led him into oil brokerage and independent production. His early business partner was W. R. Ramsey. Away from the oilfields, he served as a director of Liberty National Bank and belonged to the American Petroleum Institute. He was recognisable by a rose in his lapel and a gold-tipped walking stick.
